title: GPU fleet, capacity, IaC & CI/CD — comprehensive infra guide
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's infrastructure engineering guidance for GPU fleet capacity planning, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines and build, and operational runbooks. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners who operate or onboard teams to the GPU-serving platform.

Goals
- Provide a single reference for capacity and scaling decisions for inference workloads.
- Describe recommended Terraform modules and IaC patterns used across cloud accounts.
- Document CI/CD and build best practices for safe module and runtime changes.
- Provide runbooks and playbooks for common operational tasks and incident response.

Scope
- Applies to hosted GPU fleet (Dedicated pools and private deployments) and their control plane interactions.
- Includes GCP and AWS account patterns used in 2024-2026.
- Covers Terraform module interfaces, pipeline conventions, and operational thresholds.

Owner & Contact
- Primary owner_team: engineering (Infra & Platform).
- Document owner: Avery Chen (infra eng).
- Oncall escalation: see runbooks "oncall-and-incident-response" directory.

1) Capacity planning & GPU fleet model

Summary
- Capacity planning balances throughput (tokens/sec), latency SLOs, and cost. Fleet is organized into capacity pools by tenant-profile and hardware class (e.g., a2-highgpu, p4d, h100).

Key definitions
- Pool: logical group of similar GPU nodes with a capacity reservation.
- Headroom: percent of pool reserved for sudden bursts (standard default: 20%).
- Provision target: target utilization range for autoscale (steady-state target: 40-65%).

SLO & thresholds (examples)
- 99th-percentile latency SLO (inference path): 150ms for small requests, 500ms for long-form generation (configurable per route).
- Pool autoscale triggers: scale up at sustained 70% GPU utilization over 5 minutes; scale down after 15 minutes under 35% utilization.
- Emergency headroom: maintain 10% always available for critical customers.

Capacity planning process (quarterly)
1. Gather traffic patterns by route/model from Redwood Console.
2. Run simulated workloads with perf-suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
3. Produce capacity forecast (3/6/12 month) with scenario analysis (growth, model swap, major enterprise onboarding).
4. Submit reservation requests to finance + cloud accounts for committed capacity.

Sizing worksheet (example columns)
- Model name | Avg reqs/sec | Avg tokens/req | Peak concurrency | GPU type | GPUs required | Buffer %
- Example: redwood-13b | 15 | 300 | 120 | h100-80GB | 6 | 20%

2) Cloud accounts & networking patterns

Account topology (high-level)
- Management account (billing + org policies).
- Shared infra accounts (monitoring, CI/CD artifacts, central VPC endpoints).
- Prod workload accounts (per-region, per-environment where isolation is required).
- Private deployment accounts tenant-specific (customer-managed VPCs).

Networking guidelines
- Use centralized VPC peering / Transit Gateway for control-plane connectivity.
- Private endpoints for control-plane APIs; no public internet required for intra-fleet control traffic.
- Subnet segmentation: management, runtime, storage (NVMe/ephemeral), and egress.
- Security groups: strict least-privilege for SSH/RDP (bastion-only) and only necessary ports for model-serving runtime (gRPC/HTTP high-ports).

IP and port hygiene checklist
- Reserve CIDR blocks per account (avoid overlap).
- NAT for egress from runtime subnets with logging enabled.
- Flow logs enabled for top 3 critical subnets.

3) Terraform / IaC module patterns

Design principles
- Single responsibility modules (network, compute, autoscaler, iam).
- Strong input validation and idempotent outputs.
- Versioned modules with backwards-compatible change rules.

Canonical modules (examples)
- module/networking: creates VPC, subnets (management, runtime, storage), route tables, flow logs.
- module/gpu_cluster: autoscaling group or node-pool, GPU image config, instance templates, disk config.
- module/iam_roles: minimal runtime roles, KMS access, logging.
- module/control_plane_endpoints: private endpoint, DNS, cert management.

Module interface recommendations
- Inputs: name_prefix, environment, region, availability_zones (list string), instance_profile, instance_type, tags (map string).
- Outputs: id, primary_subnet_ids (list string), cluster_name, autoscaler_policy_id.

Example snippet (Terraform 1.5+ HCL style)
```
module "gpu_cluster" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.internal/infra/modules/gpu_cluster.git//v1.3"
  name_prefix = "redwood-prod"
  environment = "prod"
  region = "us-west1"
  instance_type = "h100-80g"
  desired_gpus = 12
}
```

Versioning & release rules
- Module semver: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Breaking changes require major bump and documented migration guide.
- PRs that change module interfaces must include an upgrade plan and test in a staging account.
- Registry: module tags pushed to internal module registry with changelog.

4) CI/CD & build pipelines

Pipeline categories
- Infrastructure module pipelines: lint, unit tests (tflint, checkov), plan against a sandbox account, and gated apply to staging/prod via manual approval.
- Runtime image build pipelines: base image build (packer/ko/cos), integration tests, image promotion.
- Control-plane deploy pipelines: deploy via blue/green or canary where supported.

Conventions & gating
- All infra PRs must run: terraform validate, tflint, tfsec/checkov, terraform plan. Plan output uploaded to a secure artifact store.
- Promotion flow: dev -> staging (auto apply) -> prod (manual approval + canary apply).
- Secrets: stored in KMS/HSM-backed secret manager with least-privilege access by pipeline service accounts.

Pipeline example (GitHub Actions style)
- Job: validate (runs tf validate + tflint)
- Job: plan (runs terraform plan against sandbox) -> uploads plan artifact
- Approval step for prod -> apply job runs in a short-lived runner with cloud credentials injected from vault.

5) Runbooks & operational playbooks

Common runbooks (links to team pages)
- GPU node replacement (runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026).
- Scale pool on-demand (emergency scaling procedure).
- Kernel or CUDA driver rollback.
- Lost KV cache recovery (serving-runtime).

Emergency scaling procedure (short)
1. Identify impacted pool in Redwood Console (check 95/99 p99 latency, queue depth).
2. If autoscaler failed, manually increase desired count: terraform state + run module/gpu_cluster -> set desired_gpus or use cloud console to scale instances.
3. Monitor until queue drained; alert SRE and the duty engineer.
4. Reconcile desired state in Terraform after incident to avoid drift.

Incident postmortem checklist
- Timeline, root cause, mitigation, customer impact, follow-ups, and owners.
- Action items: low/medium/high priority with target dates and assignees.

6) Upgrades, rollbacks & migrations

Kernel / driver upgrades
- Always test driver upgrades in canary zone with 5% of fleet.
- Validate with perf-suite: p99 latency, throughput and memory stability.
- Rollback plan: automated script to switch to previous image and drain/restart nodes.

Terraform changes & state migrations
- Use remote state (backend) with locking enabled.
- For sensitive operations (network refactor, subnet reallocation), coordinate maintenance window and communicate to product teams.
- Run terraform plan in a dry-run account and perform a canary apply (one AZ) before global apply.

7) Operational metrics & dashboards

Minimum dashboards to maintain
- Fleet overview: GPU utilization, average queue depth, pod/node restarts, disk pressure.
- Per-pool: p50/p95/p99 latency, requests/sec, tokens/sec, error rates.
- Cost dashboard: cost per token, cost per model, reserved vs spot usage.

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- GPU Utilization sustained > 85% for 10 minutes -> P1 (Scale or investigate).
- Queue depth > 500 requests -> P1.
- Disk I/O error rate > 1% -> P2.

Appendix A — Terraform module matrix
| Module | Primary inputs | Outputs | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| networking | region, azs, cidr_block | vpc_id, subnet_ids | flow logs enabled by default |
| gpu_cluster | instance_type, desired_gpus | cluster_id, autoscaler_id | supports spot + reserved strategy |
| iam_roles | principals, policies | role_arn | minimal default policies, extend per-service |

Appendix B — Quick commands
- Terraform plan for module: terraform -chdir=modules/gpu_cluster init && terraform plan -var 'environment=staging'
- Force replace an instance (GCP): gcloud compute instances reset INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
- Check GPU driver version: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
